The tone of the email is polite and professional, but it is somewhat generic and lacks specific details that would strengthen the request. To improve it, you should specify the new deadline you are requesting, briefly mention the nature of the circumstances (without oversharing), and express willingness to provide documentation if necessary. This demonstrates responsibility and respect for the professor's time.

Here is a revised version with a more proactive and respectful tone:

Subject: Request for Extension: Term Paper - [Your Name]

Dear Professor Smith,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to respectfully request a short extension on my term paper, currently due on [Original Date].

Due to unforeseen personal circumstances, I have been unable to complete the paper to the standard I aim for by the original deadline. I am committed to submitting high-quality work and would greatly appreciate an extension until [New Proposed Date].

I understand the importance of adhering to deadlines and apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. Please let me know if this extension is possible or if you require any additional information.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]
[Your Student ID]

***

The country famous for the Great Barrier Reef is Australia.
